title: How big is Africa, really?
hook: On a Mercator map Africa looks smaller than it is. Try fitting the giants inside it.

knows: that Africa is big on a map
that the US, China and India are large countries
doesNotKnow: that Africa's area exceeds the US, China and India combined
that the familiar map makes northern countries look bigger

misconception: Africa is about as big as one big country.
objective: The learner can explain that the US, China and India together cover only about three quarters of Africa's area (about 22 of 30 million km²), and that an equal-area map shows this while Mercator hides it.

claims.text: The US (lower 48 and Alaska), China and India together cover about 22.0 million km², about 73% of Africa's 30.0 million km², so the three fit inside Africa with about 8.0 million km² to spare.
claims.source: d3-geo geoArea x 6,371.0088² on the kit's 1:110m shapes, computed in Demo.tsx: US lower 48 7.98 + Alaska 1.48 (the US's two largest polygons; Hawaii and small islands, 0.04 M km², are not moved), China 9.41 (including Hainan), India 3.15, total 22.01; Africa = 51 shapes listed in africa.json, 30.04 (builder's node check, 2026-10-13). Published areas (CIA World Factbook: US 9.83, China 9.60, India 3.29; Africa about 30.4 million km²; from memory, not checked online) give about 74%. The lesson says 'about'. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 4): Re-ran in node with d3-geo geoArea x 6371.0088^2 on the kit's 110m shapes: lower 48 7.98, Alaska 1.48, China 9.41, India 3.15 = 22.01 M km2; Africa (51 shapes in africa.json) 30.04; 73.3%; room 8.03. Published areas (US 9.83 total, China 9.60, India 3.29, Africa about 30.4 M km2 incl. islands) give about 75%, so 'about 73%' on coarse shapes is within 2 points; wording says 'about' and the stage names the shapes.

claims.text: Moving a country across the globe by a rotation on the sphere does not change its size.
claims.source: Rotations of the sphere preserve area; place() in Demo.tsx composes d3-geo geoRotation calls (the kit's moveToLatitude uses the same method). Areas of the moved pieces are measured after the move. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 4): Rotations of the sphere are isometries and preserve area; place() composes geoRotation only. Node confirms the moved pieces' geoArea equals the originals.

claims.text: On an Equal Earth map, drawn areas are proportional to true areas.
claims.source: Šavrič, Patterson & Jenny (2018), The Equal Earth map projection, IJGIS 33(3) (cited in mercator-greenland, verified there). From memory for this lesson. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 4): Equal Earth is an equal-area pseudocylindrical projection (Savric, Patterson and Jenny 2018, Int. J. Geographical Information Science 33(3):454-465).

claims.text: The placement shown fits the three countries inside Africa with about 3% of the pieces overlapping a coast or each other; the fit is by total area, not an exact tiling.
claims.source: gen.mjs (committed alongside) searches rigid moves on a 0.5° raster of Africa; it reports the share of sample points outside Africa or on another piece (outsidePct in placements.json). The shown placement is one search result, chosen to illustrate the area comparison; the answer rests on c1, not on the placement. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 4): placements.json outsidePct = 2.57, shown as 'About 3%' (Math.round). The lesson says the placement is a search result and the answer rests on the total area.

claims.text: On a Mercator map the US and China, farther from the equator than most of Africa, are inflated more, which hides this.
claims.source: Mercator area scale sec² φ (Snyder 1987, ch. 7; verified in mercator-greenland c4). Centroids: contiguous US about 40°N, China about 36°N, Africa mostly within 35° of the equator. Not shown on this stage (no Mercator view); stated in the reveal. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 4): Mercator area scale is sec^2(lat) (Snyder ch. 7): about 1.7 at 40N (contiguous US), 1.5 at 35N (China), versus about 1.0-1.5 across most of Africa (which lies mostly within 35 deg of the equator). The stage has no Mercator view; stated only in the reveal.

claims.text: On a Mercator map Africa looks smaller than it is.
claims.source: Hook. Reworded from a perception claim that had no source. | Builder fix 2026-10-13 (pass 4): hook reworded to the Mercator claim (sec^2 lat inflation toward the poles; Snyder 1987). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 5): verified as a relative statement (Mercator inflates by sec^2 lat, more at the US/China/Russia latitudes than at Africa's; Africa itself is drawn at or above true scale). Wording 'smaller than it is' is only true next to far-from-equator countries; suggested hook: 'On a Mercator map Africa looks smaller than it is next to the US and China.' Not blocking.

recall.question: Which is bigger in area: Africa, or the US, China and India put together?
options: Africa, with about a quarter to spare
recall.why: The three cover about 22 million km², Africa about 30 million: they fill under three quarters of it.
